label: Home
story: Step 1 · Home DSC-001 · GOV-011 · §14.1 Home · §2.3 principles The visitor lands on the home page. The hero states what DevNepal is and is not; the platform sheet shows real numbers; then every navigation destination is summarised once — government projects, ways to contribute, community projects, people, writing — and the page closes with one call for contributors and one for ministries.

label: How to contribute
story: Step 2 · How to contribute §14.1 About · §2.2 vision · §5.2 exclusions · §12 security contact · §13 code of conduct They open “How to contribute”: mission, the four-step process, what DevNepal is not, every policy in one table, FAQ, and the support and security contacts.

label: Project detail (public)
story: Step 3 · A government project, as the public sees it GOV-007 · GOV-011 · DSC-001 · DSC-009 · App. A They open a featured project. The Official badge, named maintainers, project sheet, maintainer activity and starter tasks that link out to GitHub make the model concrete.

label: Government projects catalog
story: Step 1 · Government projects catalog DSC-001 · DSC-002 · DSC-003 · GOV-007 · GOV-010 Search and filters — ministry, contribution type, difficulty, effort, status, documentation language — narrow 18 open projects. Every card shows mode, effort and first-response time before a click. Devanagari and Latin search both work.

label: Project detail
story: Step 2 · Project detail GOV-002 · GOV-007 · GOV-008 · DSC-005 · DSC-009 · App. A The project sheet answers the four questions — how, how much, how fast they reply, until when — plus workstreams with places, starter tasks and the communication channel. The primary action reads “Sign in to apply”.

label: Sign in to apply
story: Step 3 · Sign in to apply AUTH-001 · AUTH-002 · MEM-003 · §14.3 Deciding to act opens sign-in over the same page: Google, GitHub or Facebook (per policy). The dialog explains that signing in is not the same as connecting GitHub, and that email is never public.

label: Tech blogs
story: Step 1 · Tech blogs BLG-004 · BLG-005 · BLG-007 · §14.3 Member, Official and External posts in one stream, filterable by language, topic and project.

label: Blog post
story: Step 2 · Reading a post BLG-002 · BLG-003 · BLG-004 · BLG-006 · MEM-007 A post as readers see it: labelled Member, language and reading time, described images, code and tables from safe Markdown, external links marked, the author’s verified standing beside it, a Report action.

label: Members directory
story: Step 3 · Members directory §14.1 Members · MEM-003 · MEM-004 · REC-003 People who opted in, searchable by skill, interest, province, experience and what they are open to. Prestige tiers are visible; contact details are not.

label: Member profile
story: Step 4 · A member profile MEM-002 · MEM-003 · MEM-005 · MEM-006 · GIT-009 · GIT-010 · REC-007 Verified contributions with who accepted them and how they arrived, government and community projects in separate sections, blogs, the Devs.Nepal badge set, a consented GitHub summary — and a clear list of what stays private.

label: Community projects
story: Step 5 · Community projects PPR-003 · PPR-004 · PPR-005 · MEM-007 Member-owned projects, clearly separated from government ones: neutral tag, standing disclaimer, ownership verified or not, external links marked.

label: Recognition leaderboard
story: Step 6 · Recognition · leaderboard REC-001 · REC-002 · REC-003 · REC-004 · REC-006 · REC-008 · GIT-008 Verified-impact rankings with the breakdown by contribution type, what counts and what does not, period and view toggles, and the opt-out note.

label: Badges and prestige tiers
story: Step 7 · Badges and prestige tiers REC-007 · REC-008 · §14.1 Recognition The Devs.Nepal badge set: MVP and Ambassador granted by the Office of the Prime Minister, earnable community badges, security-research badges — each with its Nepali name and how to earn it.

label: Sign in
story: Step 1 · Sign in AUTH-001 · AUTH-002 · MEM-003 Kritika hit “Sign in to apply” on a project. Google, GitHub or Facebook; the dialog separates signing in from connecting GitHub, and says email is never public.

label: Create account
story: Step 2 · Create account MEM-001 · MEM-003 · AUTH-008 · NTF-002 · §14.3 Username (public, changeable), interface language with Nepali offered first, and consent to terms and the privacy notice. Provider data is shown with its default visibility before she agrees.

label: Profile
story: Step 3 · Profile MEM-002 · MEM-004 · MEM-009 Skills from the admin taxonomy with a suggest path, experience, availability, city-level location, contribution preferences and interests. Optional fields stay optional.

label: Visibility
story: Step 4 · Visibility MEM-003 · REC-004 · GIT-009 Every field, three settings; private-always rows are locked and say so. “Members” is explained; ministries never see private fields.

label: Connect GitHub
story: Step 5 · Connect GitHub GIT-001 · GIT-002 · GIT-003 · GIT-010 · GIT-011 · REC-008 Why connect, what is read, what never. Minimum-scope GitHub App; repository selection happens on GitHub; skipping is a real option.

label: GitHub connected
story: Step 6 · Connected · first sync AUTH-008 · GIT-009 · REC-001 The connection record in full — account, scopes, time, repositories, sync state — and consent before the activity summary is shown anywhere.

label: Preview profile
story: Step 7 · Preview as a visitor MEM-008 · MEM-003 The public profile rendered exactly, beside the list of what stays hidden. Nothing was visible until now.

label: Resume with recommendations
story: Step 8 · Back where she started DSC-010 · DSC-004 Returned to the project she wanted, now able to apply, with first recommendations that explain themselves from the profile she just wrote.

label: Catalog with recommendations
story: Step 1 · Catalog with recommendations DSC-002 · DSC-010 · GOV-007 Filters mirror her profile; the recommended card explains itself (“because you listed React, ARIA…”).

label: Project detail
story: Step 2 · Project detail GOV-002 · GOV-007 · GOV-008 · DSC-009 · App. A Mode, effort, first-response SLA, deadline, repository, prerequisites; workstreams with open places; maintainer activity; starter tasks linking to GitHub.

label: Apply to a workstream
story: Step 3 · Apply to a workstream DSC-005 · DSC-006 · NTF-001 Two ministry-configured questions; the dialog states exactly what is shared with DoIT — public profile and these answers, nothing else.

label: Accepted, start work
story: Step 4 · Accepted — where to begin DSC-007 · DSC-008 · MEM-007 · GIT-003 Rajan’s acceptance with the starter task, the external hand-off to GitHub, and a readiness card confirming GitHub is connected so merged work will count.

label: Contribute
story: Step 5 · Contribute — on GitHub, or as evidence GIT-003 · GIT-007 · GIT-008 · GOV-008 · REC-008 Pull request, review and merge happen on GitHub (external). Designers, writers and testers submit evidence instead; both produce the same candidate record.

label: Submit evidence
story: Step 6 · Submit evidence · the non-code path GOV-003 · GOV-008 · REC-008 Designers, writers, testers and researchers submit a file or link with what they did; it becomes the same candidate record a merged pull request does.

label: Candidate record
story: Step 7 · Candidate record GIT-004 · GIT-005 · GIT-006 · GIT-012 · NTF-001 The merge arrives as a candidate: signature verified, de-duplicated, actor mapped, provenance kept. Visible to her and to DoIT; no score until accepted.

label: Recognised
story: Step 8 · First verified record REC-001 · REC-005 · REC-007 · MEM-005 Sabina accepted it: one row with who accepted and how it arrived, the First-accepted badge proposal, a score under the public policy, and the next task.

label: List a community project
story: Step 1 · List a community project · the rules PPR-003 · §6.3 It must be yours, no government branding, safe links only — with the reasons, before the form.

label: Project details
story: Step 2 · Details PPR-002 · ADM-001 Title with a live branding check, summary, role, status, dates, licence, taxonomy skills, images with descriptions.

label: Links checked
story: Step 3 · Links MEM-007 · PPR-005 Every link validated, normalised and labelled external; a third-party download is refused with the reason.

label: Ownership verification
story: Step 4 · Ownership verification PPR-004 · GIT-002 · GIT-003 Automatic via the connected GitHub account; domain proof optional; manual review as the fallback that still lists, as unverified.

label: Preview and publish
story: Step 5 · Preview and publish PPR-003 · REC-001 The card exactly as visitors will see it, under the standing “not government projects” notice; never appears in the government catalog or scoring.

label: Listing live
story: Step 6 · Live PPR-001 · PPR-005 · DSC-003 Listed, indexed in both scripts, on his profile; re-checks scheduled; report path open.

label: My community projects
story: Step 7 · Manage the listing PPR-001 · PPR-006 Edit, unpublish or archive; changing the repository re-runs verification, changing the title re-runs the branding check; collaboration invites are a labelled Phase 2.

label: Ownership verification lapsed
story: Step 8 · When the repository moves PPR-004 · GIT-003 GitHub reports a transfer; the badge drops to “not verified”, the owner is told why, and one click on the new repository restores it.

label: Member profile with badges
story: Step 9 · The profile as a portfolio MEM-005 · MEM-006 · GIT-009 · REC-007 Verified contributions with accepter and provenance, government and community projects apart, blogs, the badge set with earn dates, consented GitHub summary, private things stated as private.

label: Recognition settings
story: Step 10 · Recognition settings REC-003 · REC-004 · AUTH-010 Leaderboard listing, score and badge visibility as explicit choices, with what changes and what stays; private recognition history with every correction.

label: New post
story: Step 1 · New post BLG-001 · BLG-005 · BLG-007 Write on DevNepal, or link an article published elsewhere; the ground rules stated first.

label: Editor
story: Step 2 · Editor BLG-002 · BLG-004 · ADM-001 Safe Markdown with code, tables, images and links; title, language, excerpt, tags and cover with required description alongside.

label: Preview and checks
story: Step 3 · Preview and checks BLG-003 · §14.2 Rendered, sanitised preview; what was removed; accessibility issues that block or warn — one image without a description.

label: Publish
story: Step 4 · Publish BLG-001 · BLG-004 · DSC-003 Language, date, canonical URL, stable address, and what the Member label means.

label: Post live
story: Step 5 · Post live BLG-002 · BLG-004 · BLG-006 · MEM-007 As readers see it: labelled, described images, code and tables, external links marked, the author’s verified standing, a Report action.

label: Link an external article
story: Step 6 · Link an external article BLG-005 · MEM-007 Metadata fetched, rights confirmed, listed as External · Medium with the original as canonical; import deferred to Phase 2.

label: My blog posts
story: Step 7 · My posts BLG-001 · BLG-006 · §5.2 Edit as a new version, unpublish (address stays), archive; version history for moderators; no public engagement counts.

label: Profile and visibility
story: Step 1 · Profile & visibility MEM-003 · REC-004 The same per-field table from onboarding, editable any time; private-always rows locked.

label: Connections and data
story: Step 2 · Connections & data GIT-011 · AUTH-008 · AUTH-010 · §12 Disconnect GitHub with the consequences spelled out; request an export; delete the account with what the law keeps.

label: Email preferences
story: Step 3 · Email preferences NTF-001 · NTF-002 · NTF-003 · NTF-004 Five categories, two of them un-mutable; digest frequency per category; safe subject lines; no duplicate notices.

label: Recognition settings
story: Step 4 · Recognition settings REC-003 · REC-004 Leave or join the public leaderboard; hide the score; keep the private history and export it.

label: Notifications and dashboard
story: Step 5 · Dashboard and notifications NTF-001 · NTF-002 · DSC-004 · DSC-008 · DSC-010 · AUTH-008 Tasks that need her, applications, connection health, recommendations with reasons, notifications with the un-mutable security notice, and a privacy summary.

label: Report a listing
story: Step 1 · Report a listing ADM-003 · MEM-010 · PPR-005 · §12 Structured reasons across profiles, projects, posts, links and evidence; security concerns routed to the disclosure path; reporter identity visible to moderators only.

label: Fix and request reinstatement
story: Step 2 · Notice, fix and request reinstatement ADM-004 · ADM-007 · NTF-003 · PPR-003 The subject sees the reason and the three named problems; inline checks confirm each fix; appeal stays open alongside.

label: Reinstated
story: Step 3 · Reinstated ADM-007 · BLG-006 pattern · NTF-001 Back at the same address after a different moderator’s review; the warning stays on the private record only; reporters told the case is closed.

label: Recognition correction and appeal
story: Step 4 · A recognition correction, with appeal REC-005 · REC-006 · ADM-007 · §14.2 A correction reads as bookkeeping: consolidated record, the reason, before and after, and an appeal reviewed by a different Super Admin.

label: Application timeline
story: Step 5 · The application timeline — and the door out DSC-008 · DSC-005 · REC-005 Every step of an application in one place, visible to the member and the ministry: applied, accepted, opened, merged, verified, badged, scored — with a Withdraw action.

label: Invitation
story: Step 1 · Invitation · confirm the mailbox AUTH-005 · §4.2 control The email names who invited her and on what basis; a code to the official mailbox proves the address before any credential exists.

label: Enrol MFA
story: Step 2 · Enrol MFA AUTH-005 · AUTH-007 Authenticator app first, SMS fallback to the mobile from the letter, backup codes shown once. No skip.

label: Publisher terms
story: Step 3 · Publisher terms §4.2 · GOV-005 · GOV-012 · §13 Five commitments — personal account, attribution, suitability, responsiveness, code of conduct — accepted as a recorded act.

label: Ministry dashboard · first look
story: Step 4 · An empty ministry, ready to draft AUTH-004 · GOV-001 Organization, role and MFA state named; first draft one click away; officers listed with the proper way to add a colleague.

label: Officers · request a colleague
story: Step 5 · Request a second officer AUTH-004 · §4.2 matrix Sarita requests Kabir; PMO approves against a nomination and invites him through the same three steps. No password changes hands.

label: Pre-flight
story: Step 1 · Pre-flight §5.3 · GOV-001 · App. B What a listing needs, before the first field: named maintainers, a DHM-owned repository with the App installed, licence and rights, classification, bilingual title, repository hygiene.

label: Draft · 1 Identity
story: Step 2 · 1 · Identity GOV-002 · GOV-011 · App. A Identity · §14.3 Project ID, type, bilingual title, address, organization, owner, named maintainers; the badge is applied by PMO, never set here.

label: Draft · 2 Public value
story: Step 3 · 2 · Public value, description and planning GOV-002 · App. A Public value, Description, Planning Problem, target users, outcome, measurable indicators; summaries in both languages; description, background, limitations; milestones, dependencies, risks.

label: Draft · 3 Contribution need
story: Step 4 · 3 · Contribution need GOV-002 · GOV-007 · GOV-008 · App. A Contribution need Workstreams with type, difficulty and places; effort, capacity, deadline, location; skills from the taxonomy.

label: Draft · 4 How to contribute
story: Step 5 · 4 · How to contribute and governance GOV-007 · DSC-006 · App. A How to contribute, Governance Mode, prerequisites, starter tasks from GitHub labels, channel, response commitment, screening questions, code of conduct; decision model, merge authority, ownership, escalation, completion criteria.

label: Draft · 5 Technical
story: Step 6 · 5 · Technical · repository and readiness GIT-001 · GIT-003 · App. A Technical · App. B Repository connected through the GitHub App; the Appendix B readiness check runs automatically — one item fails and is fixed before submission.

label: Draft · 6 Rights, security and data
story: Step 7 · 6 · Rights, security and data GOV-002 · GOV-003 · GOV-006 · §5.3 · App. A Rights, Security and data, Attachments Approved SPDX licence, content licence, sign-off model, third-party rights, data classification (only Public is listable), security contact, disclosure URL, prohibited-data statement, readiness confirmation; the suitability rail alongside.

label: Draft · 7 Review and submit
story: Step 8 · 7 · Review and submit GOV-004 · §5.3 · §6.1 The listing as the public will see it, without the badge; the checklist at 10 of 10; a signed confirmation that the process was completed and responsibility stays with DHM.

label: In review
story: Step 9 · In review §6.1 In review · GOV-005 Submitted; the review timeline, what PMO checks, and what the ministry may still do.

label: Changes requested · resubmit
story: Step 10 · Changes requested · fix and resubmit §6.1 Changes requested · GOV-005 PMO’s reason at the top; fixes made on GitHub are re-checked, not trusted; the version increments and the thread keeps both sides.

label: Live
story: Step 11 · Live, badged GOV-011 · DSC-003 · DSC-009 · NTF-001 At the scheduled minute the listing is Open for contribution with the Official badge; the platform’s notes show the audit entry, indexing, SLA clock and notifications.

label: Ministry overview
story: Step 1 · Ministry overview with the SLA flag GOV-012 · DSC-007 · ADM-006 Open projects, applications awaiting response with the past-SLA count, candidates to verify, median first response; the flag names who has waited too long.

label: Application detail
story: Step 2 · Application detail · respond DSC-005 · DSC-006 · DSC-007 · DSC-008 · NTF-001 The applicant’s public profile and answers, the response deadline, one decision from four, an editable template; recorded under his name.

label: Applications and updates at day 30
story: Step 3 · Keeping up · day 30 GOV-009 · GOV-012 · DSC-007 Applications with deadlines attached, first PRs on GitHub, median response as a living number, and the first progress update.

label: Verification queue
story: Step 1 · Verification queue · a merged pull request GIT-007 · GIT-008 · GIT-012 · REC-005 · REC-006 Candidates from GitHub with their automatic checks; accept, request clarification or reject; separation of duties enforced.

label: Evidence review
story: Step 2 · Evidence submission · a QA report GOV-008 · REC-008 · GOV-003 Non-code work — file or link — reviewed with the same three decisions and the same record.

label: Recognition review · maintainer response
story: Step 3 · A recognition question from PMO REC-006 · REC-002 When the platform holds a burst of records, the maintainer explains and proposes; PMO decides.

label: Progress update
story: Step 1 · Progress updates GOV-009 · GOV-010 Milestone status, release links and a bilingual note on the public Updates tab; the deadline will ask, never act.

label: Lifecycle actions
story: Step 2 · Lifecycle actions GOV-004 · GOV-006 · GOV-010 · §6.1 Extend, pause, complete, cancel, archive — each with its consequence for volunteers; material edits return the listing to review; a state history under named people.

label: Completion summary
story: Step 3 · Completion summary GOV-009 · App. A Closure · REC-001 Outcome in both languages, deliverables, impact, lessons and credited contributors from verified records.

label: Ministry analytics
story: Step 4 · Analytics · own ministry §4.2 analytics · §3.2 · ADM-006 Applications, response, verified contributions by type, inclusion — for DoIT projects only, privacy-safe.

label: Publish as the ministry
story: Step 1 · Publish as DoIT BLG-007 · AUTH-007 · §4.2 The Official option exists only for officers PMO granted it to; it ties the post to a project and asks for re-authentication.

label: Audit log · my actions
story: Step 2 · Audit log · my actions GOV-005 · ADM-008 Every draft, submission, response, verification and post under his name and time — the same view PMO sees, filtered to him.

label: Onboarding request
story: Step 1 · Onboarding request · the nomination letter AUTH-004 · §4.2 control A Secretary’s letter logged as a request: domain check, named person, signatory verified by phone, no duplicate organization.

label: Provision ministry
story: Step 2 · Provision the organization and its first officer AUTH-004 · AUTH-005 · ADM-001 One dialog, two records; email must match the domain; MFA is a fact, not an option; the letter is cited in the audit entry.

label: Officer request approval
story: Step 3 · Approve a second officer AUTH-004 · §4.2 matrix A publisher requested a colleague; PMO checks domain, named person, nomination, requester’s standing — and invites through the same three steps.

label: Revoke officer access
story: Step 4 · Revoke an officer AUTH-007 · AUTH-009 · GOV-005 · ADM-008 A transfer: sessions end immediately, drafts stay with the ministry, attribution survives, the organization must keep at least one active officer.

label: Audit log
story: Step 5 · Audit log · the organization’s whole story GOV-005 · ADM-005 · ADM-008 Every step wrote one line: request, provisioning, acceptance, officer changes, submissions, publications, revocation — append-only, exports logged.

label: Review queue
story: Step 1 · Review queue with the selected submission ADM-002 · GOV-005 · §5.3 · §6.1 Queue, filters, assignment and SLA beside the detail: suitability checklist with a reviewer note, attachments, version diff, and three decisions.

label: Request changes
story: Step 2 · Request changes GOV-005 · §6.1 Changes requested · ADM-008 The checklist is complete but a reviewer note flags credentials in the docs; the reason is mandatory and travels to the ministry verbatim.

label: Approve and schedule
story: Step 3 · Approve and schedule GOV-011 · §6.1 Approved / scheduled · GOV-005 Approval and publication are separate decisions; the badge is bound to this act; scheduling aligns with the ministry’s announcement.

label: Published
story: Step 4 · Published, badged GOV-011 · DSC-003 · NTF-001 The listing as the public sees it, with the platform’s notes: state change with the approver’s name, badge, indexing, SLA clock, notifications.

label: Triage
story: Step 1 · Triage · the report becomes a case PPR-005 · ADM-003 · BLG-006 pattern Snapshot frozen, link and image checks, related reports merged, severity suggested; a person decides.

label: Moderation queue
story: Step 2 · Moderation queue and case ADM-002 · ADM-004 · ADM-005 Queue with filters and SLA, the frozen snapshot, reporters visible to moderators only, an interim hide that is itself logged.

label: Decide
story: Step 3 · Decide with a reason ADM-004 · AUTH-007 · ADM-008 Six possible actions, one chosen; taxonomy reason plus her words; preview of what the member will read; what will happen, listed.

label: Notices sent
story: Step 4 · Both sides notified, differently NTF-001 · NTF-002 · NTF-003 · ADM-007 Subject gets the full reason and options; reporters learn action was taken; public sees “unavailable”; safe subject lines.

label: Second review
story: Step 5 · Second review · a different moderator ADM-007 · REC-006 pattern Original decision, before/after, the member’s note; reinstate, uphold or modify — with reason; warning retention stated.

label: Blog post case
story: Step 6 · A blog post case BLG-006 · ADM-004 · §13 Reports on posts join the same queue; what is specific: version history is the evidence and “copied content” checks against the canonical source. Escalation to legal is one of the six actions.

label: Community health
story: Step 7 · Community health §3.2 community health · ADM-006 Cases by reason, outcome mix, turnaround, appeals, repeat subjects — aggregates only — and the pattern that becomes a product change.

label: Anomaly case
story: Step 1 · Anomaly held before display REC-006 · GIT-008 Eight merged PRs in four minutes pass integrity checks but hit the rate cap; four scored, four held; the public board is untouched.

label: Anomaly review
story: Step 2 · Review, then ask the maintainer REC-006 · REC-002 The PRs with size and timing; PMO asks rather than guesses; the policy’s blind spot becomes visible.

label: Correction
story: Step 3 · Correction with a reason REC-005 · ADM-008 Eight records consolidated into one: before/after, taxonomy reason, the member’s notice previewed; reversible.

label: Badge record
story: Step 4 · Badge record · re-evaluation REC-007 A count badge follows its evidence: criteria, issue, re-evaluation, revocation state; ministry badges need a human to revoke.

label: Scoring policy editor
story: Step 5 · Scoring policy editor · v1.3 draft REC-002 · REC-008 · ADM-001 Weights and caps in one place, a batch rule from the case, public changelog, effective date, product-owner approval required.

label: Public scoring policy
story: Step 6 · Public scoring policy REC-001 · REC-002 What anyone can read: active version, weights, caps, exclusions, changelog and aggregate corrections.

label: Operational dashboard
story: Step 1 · Operational dashboard ADM-006 · §3.2 Exception tiles with owners and ages — stale projects, sync failures, applications past SLA, open queues — over adoption metrics.

label: Stale project
story: Step 2 · Stale project escalation GOV-010 · GOV-012 · DSC-009 A paused project with waiting volunteers; PMO nudges, escalates and flags — it never edits the ministry’s listing.

label: Sync health
story: Step 3 · Sync health GIT-004 · GIT-011 Every GitHub App installation with last delivery and error; refused deliveries are the signature control working.

label: Reconciliation
story: Step 4 · Reconciliation run GIT-005 · GIT-006 · GIT-012 Missed merges recovered through the API, de-duplicated, rate-limited, provenance kept; maintainers still verify.

label: Taxonomy
story: Step 5 · Taxonomy ADM-001 · MEM-004 · §14.3 Skills, tags, types and categories: member suggestions merged, added or rejected; bilingual labels required; every change versioned.

label: Licences and badge definitions
story: Step 6 · Licences and badge definitions ADM-001 · REC-007 · §5.2 Approved SPDX licences with legal references; badge definitions with criteria, issuer and mode; versions for both.

label: Feature flags
story: Step 7 · Feature flags ADM-001 Open decisions as switches — leaderboard default, Facebook sign-in, auto-hide, readiness blocking — scoped, owned, reasoned, four-eyes where members are affected.

label: Privileged access
story: Step 8 · Privileged access and sessions AUTH-003 · AUTH-007 Three Super Admins, every session with device and place, one-click revocation, second-admin confirmation for grants, first admin from deployment.

label: Monthly report
story: Step 9 · Monthly §3.2 report §3.2 · ADM-005 Eight outcome areas, privacy-safe aggregation with a minimum cell size, a logged and purpose-limited export for the steering committee.
